record.context_brief: Operators decreasing the number of nonreal zeros
record.original_question:
Let π_n be the real vector space of all real polynomials of degree at
most n, and let Z_c(p) denote the number of
nonreal zeros of a real polynomial p, counted with multiplicity.
Characterize all linear operators T: π_n → π_n such
that Z_c(T[p]) ≤ Z_c(p) for every real polynomial p in π_n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\pi_n$ denote the real vector space of all polynomials in one variable $x$ with real coefficients of degree at most $n$. For a polynomial $p \in \pi_n$, let $Z_c(p)$ denote the number of nonreal zeros of $p$, counted with multiplicity (so that $Z_c(p) + Z_r(p) = \deg p$, where $Z_r(p)$ is the number of real zeros counted with multiplicity).

A linear operator $T: \pi_n \to \pi_n$ is called complex-zero-decreasing (on $\pi_n$) if
$$Z_c(T[p]) \le Z_c(p)$$
for every $p \in \pi_n$ (with the convention that $T[p]$ is again a real polynomial).

Problem: Give an explicit characterization of all linear operators $T: \pi_n \to \pi_n$ that are complex-zero-decreasing in the above sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The characterization of linear operators on $\pi_n$ that decrease the number of nonreal zeros is a classical problem in the Pólya–Schur–Laguerre program. Only partial results are known: characterizations of complex-zero-decreasing sequences (diagonal operators in the standard basis), and certain characterizations involving operators commuting with differentiation or acting on specific polynomial bases (e.g., Hermite). A full characterization of all such linear operators remains open.

status_evidence.title: Linear Operators and the Distribution of Zeros of Entire Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Provides characterization of multiplier sequences and complex zero decreasing sequences for various polynomial bases, indicating partial progress on the broader operator characterization problem.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial characterizations (of CZDS / multiplier sequences in particular bases) are known; the general operator characterization remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Real zero polynomials and Pólya–Schur type theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Pólya–Schur type characterizations of linear operators preserving real-rootedness and related zero-distribution properties.
status_evidence.claim: Related Pólya–Schur type problems for zero-preserving/decreasing operators are an active area with partial results.
